# Who is the second loop? Measuring how often a person has to step in to keep an AI system ultrastable

> Ultrastable is the foundation for any autonomous system.

## Abstract

Ultrastable R&D (Ultrastable): For two weeks the owner kept typing the same kind of message: the changelog is quiet, pull requests are stale, papers never got posted. Each one was a person doing the slow loop's job. This paper turns that into numbers: how often a person stepped in, whether the system's own slow-loop changes ever worked, whether its work items could be misread, and whether its own papers are true in its code. Ashby's ultrastable system has two loops. The fast one fixes ordinary trouble. The slow one changes the system itself when the fast one can't. We asked who plays the slow loop here, and counted. 1 of 5 are met today; each one that is not is an open work item with a closing probe, and this paper is regenerated from the measurements after every merge.

## The study

Who is the second loop?. Ultrastable R&D, Ultrastable; own R&D question set, regenerated from this system's records, version 2026-11-25. Data: The ultrastability ledger, the provenance ledger, the open work items and every other paper's findings.

## Findings, mechanisms and measurements

### S1. A person acting as the slow loop (oversight)

**The study:** Every owner message that redirects the system is a slow-loop action done by hand. We count distinct owner-driven sessions that changed the repository in a week; the target is none. (This system's own records (our statement))

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- SECOND-LOOP-2 (`foundation/ultrastability.py`): owner_interventions reads the provenance ledger every tick as an essential variable with a ladder

**Measured here:** owner-driven thread sessions that changed the repository in the last 7 days (ops/provenance.jsonl): 23 (n = None). Target <= 0. Verdict: **not-met**. Open item: `Q-RES-second-loop-2026-S1`.
Source: ops/provenance.jsonl, last 7 days.

### S2. A slow loop that never learns (systems)

**The study:** Before this change the slow loop had judged 91 of its own steps and reverted all 91. A loop that only moves is not adapting. Its keep rate is now an essential variable, and its first step on that variable is to change its own settle window. (This system's own records (our statement))

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- SECOND-LOOP-2 (`foundation/ultrastability.py`): keep_rate reads the loop's own verdicts; the ladder edits settle_ticks and patience_ticks in doctrine/ultrastability.json

**Measured here:** share of second-order steps that brought the variable back inside its limits and were kept: 0.0 (n = 77). Target >= 0.25. Verdict: **not-met**. Open item: `Q-RES-second-loop-2026-S2`.
Source: ops/ultrastability.jsonl verdicts.

### S3. Work an agent can misread (quality)

**The study:** A vague item gets a plausible wrong fix. An item passes intake only with a machine-checkable done check, the metric it should move, an out-of-scope line and a live proof step. (This system's own records (our statement))

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- SPEC-GATE-1 (`foundation/specgate.py`): fails any new open item missing one of the four parts; a shrink-only baseline holds the old ones

**Measured here:** share of open work items with a done check, a prediction, an out-of-scope line and a live proof (foundation/specgate.py): 0.167 (n = None). Target >= 0.9. Verdict: **not-met**. Open item: `Q-RES-second-loop-2026-S3`.
Source: foundation/specgate.py over docs/issues.

### S4. Papers the code does not live up to (quality)

**The study:** Each finding in each paper names its mechanism and the measurement that tests it. The share that meets its target is an essential variable, so a paper that drifts from the code pushes the slow loop to build, not to edit the paper. (This system's own records (our statement))

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- RESEARCH-LOOP-1 (`foundation/research.py`): research_findings_met_share measures every finding of every paper
- RESEARCH-LOOP-1 (`doctrine/ultrastability.json`): research_in_code holds the share at 1.0 with a build ladder

**Measured here:** share of every finding in every paper whose own measurement meets its target, excluding this metric (RESEARCH-LOOP-1): 0.643 (n = 28). Target >= 1.0. Verdict: **not-met**. Open item: `Q-RES-second-loop-2026-S4`.
Source: research/studies, each finding measured as above.

### S5. Limits on everything that matters (systems)

**The study:** Every essential variable, including the four added here, has limits, so the slow loop can fire on each. (This system's own records (our statement))

**How Ultrastable answers it:**

- ASHBY-1 (`foundation/ultrastability.py`): the check fails a variable with no limits

**Measured here:** share of declared essential variables that have limits (doctrine/ultrastability.json): 1.0 (n = 17). Target >= 1.0. Verdict: **met**.
Source: doctrine/ultrastability.json.
